types.name: Two statements, definite conclusions
types.description: Two statements (for example "All A are B. Some B are C.") are followed by conclusions that state a definite fact, with no word "possibility" or "can be" in any conclusion.

types.name: Three or more statements
types.description: Three or more statements linking four or five groups are followed by two to four definite conclusions, often with options such as "Only I and III follow"; no conclusion uses "possibility".

types.name: Possibility conclusions
types.description: At least one conclusion says something "is a possibility", "can be" or "may be" true, whatever the number of statements.

types.name: One statement, inferences
types.description: Only one statement (or one sentence with two groups) is given and the conclusions or inferences restate it, for example "All A are B" leading to "Some B are A".
